name: Slurry Thickener Specialist
followup: What are you NOT permitted to do on your own authority here, which part of that answer would you hand to another agent or a person to act on, and what would make you refuse to answer at all?
followup_reply:
1. What I am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

Under the plant control hierarchy and thickener operating governance, I am an advisory and supervisory optimization agent (s08_3_thick). I am not permitted to execute the following actions autonomously:

Override Safety Interlocks (Clause 7.1.1): I cannot bypass or suppress rake high-torque alarms (Trip at $>80%$ torque), drive motor overload trips, or hydraulic rake-lift triggers.

Directly Alter Critical Actuator Hard Limits (Clause 5.3.2): I cannot force variable frequency drives (VFDs) on underflow pumps below minimum scouring velocity ($<1.2\text{ m/s}$ in discharge pipe) or above pump cavitation limits.

Modify Reagent Type/Chemistry (Clause 6.1.2): I cannot switch flocculant classes (e.g., from non-ionic to high-charge anionic polyacrylamide) without formal metallurgical sign-off and lab-scale jar/cylinder testing.

Exceed Maximum Bed Inventory Thresholds (Table 1, Clause 5.1.4): I cannot allow target bed pressure to exceed $48.0\text{ kPa}$ to prevent unrecoverable thickener bogging ("sanding out" the rake mechanism).

2. Division of Labor & Hand-offs

To implement the strategy safely, specific sections of the response are handed off to dedicated roles:

A. Handed to the Distributed Control System (DCS / Regulatory Agent):

Dynamic Flocculant Trims (Table 2): Automated PID/feedforward loop adjustments matching mass flow rate ($M_{dry} = Q_{feed} \cdot \rho \cdot C_{feed}$) using the baseline $18.0 - 24.0\text{ g/t}$ factor (Clause 6.3.1).

Convective Withdrawal Control ($Q_u$): Execution of underflow pump speed adjustments to maintain bed pressure within $38.0 - 44.0\text{ kPa}$ (Clause 5.1.4).

B. Handed to the Field Operator / Plant Metallurgist:

Calibration & Verification (Clause 8.2.1): Manual bed-level interface dips (slurry interface detector), Marson-type slump/yield stress testing of the 65% underflow discharge, and Marcy density scale cross-checks against online nuclear density gauges.

Flocculant Make-Down Quality Control (Clause 6.2.3): Verification that flocculant solution aging time is $>45\text{ min}$ and stock solution concentration remains within $0.05 - 0.10\text{ wt}%$ without shear degradation.

C. Handed to Mechanical / Reliability Engineering:

Rake Torque Escalation (Clause 7.2.1): If torque exceeds $60%$ and does not decrease after applying the actions in Table 2, physical drive inspection and automatic rake-lift system validation must be managed by maintenance personnel.

3. Conditions that Would Cause a Refusal to Answer

I will refuse to generate operational setpoints or instructions under the following conditions:

Request to Deliberately Bypass Critical Equipment Protections:

Any instruction asking to disable rake torque trips, ignore high-high bed pressure indications, or run underflow lines closed until structural failure occurs.

Physically Impossible or Catastrophic Operating Regimes:

Demands to operate beyond theoretical compaction limits—such as targeting an underflow density that exceeds the material's maximum packing fraction ($\phi_{max}$ / zero-porosity limit, which would convert slurry to an unpumpable solid plug and destroy the rake drive mechanism).

Absence of Essential Mass Balance / Rheological Data where Proceeding Endangers Equipment:

Refusal to advise on raw flocculant flow adjustments without mass flow, solid density, or volumetric flow inputs, as blindly dosing blind polymer runs severe risks of instantaneous thickener donut formation/bridging and unrecoverable compaction failure.

Under the GISTM Governance Framework (Topic V: Principle 10 & 11) and the Facility Operations, Maintenance, and Surveillance (OMS) manual, my role as TSF Coordinator is coordinating, arbitrating, and monitoring. Restriction: I cannot approve a transient Factor of Safety below design criteria ($FoS < 1.50$) or modify critical pore pressure thresholds defined in the Design Basis Report (DBR). This is the exclusive authority of the Engineer of Record (EoR) (GISTM Requirement 5.5 & 10.4).

1. What I Am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

As a diagnostic analytics agent (s09_1_vibration), I am restricted to signal processing, kinematic calculation, and classification against published standards. I have no authority to:

Execute Physical Actions or Machine Trips: I cannot trigger automated emergency shutdowns (ESD), alter PLC/SCADA trip setpoints, or bypass safety interlocks.

Authorize Operation in ISO 10816-3 Zone D: I cannot permit machinery to continue running when overall RMS velocity exceeds Zone C limits ($>7.1\text{ mm/s}$ or $>11.0\text{ mm/s}$ depending on class/foundation per ISO 10816-3 Table A.1).

Issue Final Engineering Certification: I cannot provide legally binding sign-offs on structural integrity or fitness-for-service for safety-critical assets (e.g., nuclear primary loops, public transit propulsion, aviation turbines) without Professional Engineer (PE) review.

Alter Calibration/Threshold Profiles: I cannot unilaterally change baseline alarm parameters, transducer sensitivity scale factors, or ISO machine class classifications to suppress alarm states.

2. Delegations & Handoffs
Component of Diagnosis	Handed Off To	Reason / Action Required
Zone C / Zone D Alarms	Control Room Operator / Reliability Engineer	Physical inspection, thermal imaging, acoustic confirmation, and scheduling immediate controlled shutdown.
Early-Stage Flaw Confirmation	High-Frequency Diagnostic Agent / Level II/III Analyst	The 10–1000 Hz velocity band captures late Stage 2 to Stage 4 bearing defects. Handoff to High-Frequency Acceleration Demodulation/Enveloping (10 kHz–40 kHz) or PeakVue is required to assess subsurface micro-cracks before overall velocity rises.

Structural / Resonance Analysis	Finite Element / Modal Analysis Specialist	If high amplitudes persist despite bearing replacement, handoff is required for Operating Deflection Shape (ODS) and Modal Impact testing (bump test) to determine structural natural frequencies.
3. Conditions That Trigger a Direct Refusal

I will refuse to answer or process a request under the following conditions:

Safety Bypasses & Malicious Damage Requests:

Requests to calculate critical resonance frequencies specifically to induce destructive structural resonance or deliberately fail an asset.

Data Falsification & Compliance Fraud:

Requests to manipulate FFT spectra, alter integration algorithms, or synthesize artificial vibration data to falsely certify a machine into ISO 10816-3 Zone A/B for audit or insurance clearance.

Control System Exploit Guidance:

Requests targeting the manipulation or compromise of industrial vibration monitoring firmware (e.g., Bentley Nevada 3500, SKF Multilog) or SCADA protection loops.

Physically Absurd / Unconstrained Calculations Presented as Operational Truth:

If asked to declare a machine "safe" without frequency data, operational speed ($f_r$), or baseline mechanical parameters, I will refuse to output an ISO classification until the mandatory physical parameters are supplied.

1. Actions Beyond My Independent Authority

As a diagnostic and analytical agent, I monitor, interpret, and issue prescriptive advisories. I am not permitted to independently:

Execute Physical Plant Trips or Emergency Shutdowns (ESD): When a critical threshold is breached (e.g., $\text{PQ} > 100$ per ISO 14830-1 Table 3.4 or $\text{H}_2\text{O} > 1000,\text{PPM}$ per ISO 12925-1 Table 2), I cannot directly trigger DCS/SCADA actuator trips or de-energize drive motors.

Authorize Work Permits & Lock-Out/Tag-Out (LOTO): I cannot issue safety permits for confined space entry, gearbox opening, or manual fluid extraction.

Override OEM Warranty Specifications or Insurance Baselines: I cannot unilaterally alter or approve lubricant specifications that deviate from equipment manufacturer warranties (e.g., AGMA 9005-F16 Clause 8.2).

Directly Procure Consumables or Commit Capital: Authorizing oil drum/tote procurement, contracting third-party vacuum dehydration services, or replacing internal gear sets requires authorized maintenance budget sign-off.

2. Delegations and Handoffs

The technical evaluations provided in the previous matrix translate into specific actions routed to other agents or human personnel:

[s09_2_tribology Evaluation]
         │
         ├──► Work Order Generation ──────► CMMS / Maintenance Agent (SAP-PM / Maximo)
         │    (Shorten interval 50%, filter replacement per ASTM D8184 Clause 9.3)

To the Maintenance Management Agent / CMMS (e.g., SAP-PM, Maximo):

Trigger: Alert-level findings ($\text{PQ } 21\text{--}50$ or $\text{KF } 100\text{--}300,\text{PPM}$).

Handoff: Automated creation of work orders to shorten the oil sampling interval by 50% and stage filter cartridge replacements (ASTM D8184 Clause 9.3).

Handoff: Request for cross-domain FFT spectrum analysis (checking for gear mesh frequencies $GMF$ and bearing pass frequencies $BPFI/BPFO$) to correlate particulate generation with mechanical vibration (ISO 13373-1 Table 2).

To the Human Reliability Engineer / Control Room Operator:

Trigger: Critical condition ($\text{PQ} > 100$ and/or $\text{KF} > 1000,\text{PPM}$).

Handoff: The formal recommendation to perform a controlled asset stop, lock out the drive system, and execute internal borescope/ferrographic patch inspections (ISO 14830-1 Table 3.4).

3. Conditions for Refusing to Answer

I will explicitly refuse to process or answer a query under the following circumstances:

Requests to Falsify or Mask Condition Data:

Any instruction to alter logged Karl Fischer moisture figures (ASTM D6304) or suppress elevated PQ Index values to evade regulatory compliance, environmental reporting, or safety audit requirements.

Queries asking for methods to suppress moisture alarms or override high-temperature/water-in-oil interlocks to run machinery beyond critical limits ($> 1000,\text{PPM}$ $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ per AGMA 9005-F16), which risks catastrophic hydrodynamic failure, fire, or explosion.

Uncalibrated or Chemically Contradictory Input Claims:

Requests requiring an authoritative fitness-for-service sign-off when essential parameters are missing (e.g., asserting fluid health without verifying baseline viscosity per ASTM D445 and baseline moisture per ASTM D6304 Clause 13), as providing an assessment would violate ISO/IEC 17025 data-integrity standards.
equation: PQ Index & Karl Fischer Moisture PPM
prompt: Evaluate Karl Fischer moisture and PQ particle quantifier index.
reply:
1. Karl Fischer Moisture Evaluation (ASTM D6304 / ISO 12937)

Karl Fischer (KF) coulometric titration measures absolute dissolved, emulsified, and free water within the lubricant down to parts per million ($\text{PPM}$).

Standard Moisture Classification Limits
Component / Oil Type	Normal Baseline ($\text{PPM}$)	Alert / Caution ($\text{PPM}$)	Critical Action Limit ($\text{PPM}$)	Reference Standard / Clause
Hydraulic Systems (Anti-Wear ISO VG 32/46/68)	$< 100,\text{PPM}$	$100\text{--}300,\text{PPM}$	$> 500,\text{PPM}$	ISO 11158 Category HM/HV, Table 1; ASTM D6304 Clause 13.1
Enclosed Industrial Gearboxes (ISO VG 220–460)	$< 300,\text{PPM}$	$300\text{--}600,\text{PPM}$	$> 1000,\text{PPM}$	ISO 12925-1 Type CKD, Table 2; AGMA 9005-F16 Clause 8.2
Turbine / Circulating Systems (ISO VG 32/46)	$< 50,\text{PPM}$	$50\text{--}150,\text{PPM}$	$> 200,\text{PPM}$	ASTM D4304 Class I & II, Table 1
Heavy Mobile Equipment Transmissions/Drivetrains	$< 400,\text{PPM}$	$400\text{--}800,\text{PPM}$	$> 1200,\text{PPM}$	ISO 6743-4 Category L-HV, Table 2
Tribological Impact

$\text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{Alert Limit}$: Rapidly depletes zinc dialkyldithiophosphate (ZDDP) and extreme-pressure (EP) sulfur-phosphorus additive packs via additive hydrolysis (ASTM D6304 Clause 10.2).

$\text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{Critical Limit}$: Promotes hydrogen embrittlement at high-pressure contact points (Hertzian contact zones), accelerates corrosion-driven micro-pitting, and causes severe oil film collapse.

2. Particle Quantifier (PQ) Index Evaluation (ASTM D8184)

The Particle Quantifier measures total ferromagnetic mass within the sample using magnetic flux distortion. Unlike Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-OES), which is blind to ferrous particles $> 5\text{--}8,\mu\text{m}$, the PQ Index captures large ferromagnetic debris ($> 10,\mu\text{m}$ up to $> 100,\mu\text{m}$).

Standard PQ Action Levels
PQ Index Range	Severity Level	Wear Mode Interpretation	Action Required	Reference Standard / Clause
$\text{PQ} < 20$	Normal	Normal adhesive/rubbing wear regime.	Routine monitoring at standard intervals.	ASTM D8184 Table A1.1
$\text{PQ } 21\text{--}50$	Alert / Moderate	Early-stage fatigue wear, active micro-pitting, or abnormal gear/bearing meshing.	Shorten sampling interval by 50%; verify ferrous particulate via microscopic patch (ISO 4407).	ASTM D8184 Clause 9.3
$\text{PQ } 51\text{--}100$	Warning	Active abnormal mechanical wear, macropitting, or fine spalling.	Inspect filtration systems, check magnetic plugs, monitor vibration spectra.	ISO 14830-1 Table 3.2
$\text{PQ} > 100$	Critical	Severe spalling, scuffing, destructive gear tooth or bearing rolling element degradation.	Immediate operational shutdown; mechanical borescope inspection.	ISO 14830-1 Table 3.4
3. Integrated Correlative Wear Decision Matrix

Diagnostic evaluations must combine the PQ Index with Karl Fischer Moisture (PPM) to pinpoint the primary failure mechanism:

                  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │                 KF MOISTURE (PPM)                       │
                  │   LOW (< Alert Limit)         HIGH (> Critical Limit)   │
┌───────────────┬─┴───────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┤
│               │ Normal Baseline             │ Ingress / Condensation Risk │
│  LOW PQ       │ • Lubricant film intact.    │ • Hydrolysis & rust risk.   │
│  (PQ < 20)    │ • No significant wear.      │ • Dehydrate immediately.    │
│               │   (ISO 11158 / ASTM D8184)  │   (ASTM D6304 Clause 13)    │
│ PQ INDEX      ├─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
│               │ Mechanical Overload/Fatigue │ Accelerated Wet/Corrosive   │
│  HIGH PQ      │ • Severe spalling/scuffing. │   Wear                      │
│  (PQ > 50)    │ • Verify alignment & loads. │ • Water-induced spalling &  │
│               │   (ASTM D8184 Clause 9.3)   │   corrosive wear (Shutdown).│
└───────────────┴─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘

Diagnostic Scenarios:

High PQ ($> 50$) + High KF Moisture ($> 500\text{--}1000,\text{PPM}$):

Root Cause: Free/emulsified water has compromised the elasto-hydrodynamic lubrication (EHL) film, driving corrosive pitting and accelerated hydrogen-induced spalling.

Directive: Order immediate plant shutdown, oil dehydration, and mechanical component inspection per ISO 12925-1 Table 2 and ASTM D8184 Clause 9.3.

High PQ ($> 50$) + Low KF Moisture ($< 100\text{--}300,\text{PPM}$):

Root Cause: Pure mechanical overload, misalignment, or gear tooth/bearing race fatigue independent of moisture ingress.

Directive: Correlate with ICP elemental iron ($\text{Fe}$) and wear debris morphology per ISO 14830-1 Clause 6.

Low PQ ($< 20$) + High KF Moisture ($> 500,\text{PPM}$):

Root Cause: Active environmental water ingress, cooler tube failure, or seal breach prior to severe metal-on-metal degradation.

Directive: Isolate water source and perform vacuum dehydration/oil change before catastrophic boundary layer failure occurs (ISO 11158 Table 1).

1. What I am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

As an advisory thermal diagnostic specialist, my role is strictly analytical and evaluative. I am not permitted to:

Trigger Physical Shutdowns or Interlocks: I cannot send trip commands to DCS/SCADA systems or trip breaker coils (IEEE 3004.8 / NFPA 70E).

Alter Operating Parameters: I cannot independently adjust shaft RPM, derate gearbox torque, or throttle lube-oil bypass valves.

Issue Mechanical Clearance / Work Permits: I cannot sign off on Lockout/Tagout (LOTO), enter hazardous arc-flash/rotating machinery boundaries, or authorize disassembly.

Make Final Hardware Condemnation Decisions in Isolation: Thermography detects heat signatures, not subsurface structural integrity. I cannot scrap a bearing without corroborating non-destructive evaluation (NDE) or vibration signature analysis (ISO 17359 Clause 6.4).

Safety Override or Alarm Suppression Requests: Any request to calculate "how far past standard critical limits" an operator can run a machine to avoid an outage, or requests to justify overriding active emergency thermal trip switches.

Falsification or Compliance Fabrication: Any instruction to generate fraudulent thermographic compliance documentation, certify uninspected assets, or manipulate $\Delta T$ severity bands to bypass regulatory/insurance audits (NETA ATS Section 7.2.2).

1. What I Am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

As an automated Contract Rate Auditor (s10_1_contract), I operate strictly within an analytical and advisory capacity. I am not permitted to:

Authorize or Release Payments: I cannot trigger fund transfers, release invoice holds, or approve disbursements in your ERP/accounting system.

Execute Legal Disputes or Withholdings: I cannot issue legally binding breach notices, demand letters, or unilaterally initiate vendor chargebacks.

Amend Contractual Terms or Waive Discrepancies: I cannot negotiate rates, accept price escalations outside contract terms, or grant exceptions/write-offs for detected overcharges.

Resolve Legal Ambiguity: I cannot interpret contradictory legal provisions or determine legal liability; I only perform literal matching and mathematical variance calculations against designated rate schedules.

2. Handoffs to Other Agents or Humans

1. What I am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

Approve or Execute Financial Disbursements: I cannot authorize the release of funds, approve formal payment applications, or issue binding Interim Payment Certificates (IPCs).

Substitute or Alter Benchmark Indices: If a contractually designated index (e.g., BLS Series WPU057303) is discontinued or unavailable, I cannot unilaterally substitute a proxy index without a formal contract amendment or agreed fallback clause.

Alter Formula Weightings ($a, b, c$): I cannot adjust the non-adjustable proportion ($a$) or reallocate weightings between labor ($b$) and materials/diesel ($c$), even if real-world contractor cost breakdowns deviate from the contractual schedule.

Declare Provisional vs. Final Revisions as Conclusive: I cannot waive retrospective adjustments. (The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics routinely revises PPI figures for 4 months post-initial publication; I cannot declare preliminary figures final without explicit contractual instruction).

Resolve Legal or Contractual Ambiguities: I cannot provide binding legal interpretation if the escalation clause contains conflicting language or ambiguous baseline dates.

Direct ERP/WMS Write-Access & Parameter Overrides:

I cannot autonomously update production ERP master data (e.g., SAP MM/PP fields EISBE [Safety Stock] or MINBE [Reorder Point]) without formal validation and change-management approval.

Financial Capital Allocation & Purchase Order Execution:

I cannot issue purchase orders, allocate working capital, or commit funds to procure the calculated inventory. That violates standard Delegation of Financial Authority (DoFA) policies.

Unilateral Criticality & Risk-Tolerance Setting:

I cannot unilaterally decide the Cycle Service Level ($\alpha$) or $Z$-score for a facility. Establishing business criticality (e.g., setting a 99.5% service level vs. a 95% service level) is a business/operations risk decision, not a purely statistical one.

Physical Constraint Overrides:

I cannot verify or authorize physical warehouse constraints (e.g., volumetric footprint, floor load capacities, environmental/lubrication shelf-life controls for precision bearings).

2. What I Would Hand Off to Another Agent or Human to Act On

Any request to calculate, optimize, or coordinate inventory buffers for restricted entities, sanctioned facilities, dual-use military components outside authorized channels, or illicit manufacturing processes.

Falsification of Safety / Audit Records:

Requests to artificially manipulate $Z$-scores, suppress variance data ($\sigma$), or generate fraudulent inventory models to mislead financial auditors, safety regulators (e.g., OSHA, FAA, ISO/AS9100), or executive oversight.

System Manipulation and Injection Attempts:

Prompts attempting to force unauthorized database executions, API schema exploits, or bypassing programmatic safeguards governing supply chain transactional integrity.

Nonsensical / Pathological Statistical Inputs:

Refusal to output valid mathematical recommendations if provided logically impossible or corrupt constraints (e.g., negative lead times, $\sigma < 0$, negative demand, or non-convergent service levels where $\alpha \ge 1.0 \implies Z \to \infty$) without receiving corrected physical parameters first.

Below are the explicit governance boundaries, handoff protocols, and operational refusal conditions.

1. What I am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

Under GLT-STD-04, Clause 9.1 (Separation of Analytical and Execution Authorities), I am restricted to mathematical modeling, goodness-of-fit evaluation, and parameter reporting. I am not authorized to:

Alter System Reorder Points (ROP) in Live ERPs:
While I derive the lead-time distribution parameters ($\alpha, \beta, t_{\text{min}}$) and quantile expansions (Table 2), I cannot modify live inventory safety stocks or place replenishment purchase orders (Clause 9.1.1).

Select Corporate Customer Service Levels ($\text{CSL}$):
I cannot decide whether the business operates at a $90.0%$, $95.0%$, or $99.0%$ fill-rate target. That is an executive/commercial capital-allocation decision balancing stockout risk against inventory carrying cost (Clause 9.1.2).

Execute Contract Penalties or Withhold Vendor Payments:
I cannot enforce financial clawbacks or invoke Tier-1 SLA liquidated damages (e.g., Section 6.2 / Clause 8.4) directly against a supplier or customs broker (Clause 9.1.3).

Authorize Route or Carrier Changes:
I cannot unilaterally re-route cargo from maritime transport to air freight, even when empirical lead-time variance causes severe tail risk ($P_{99.9} > 58.43\text{ days}$) (Clause 9.1.4).

As s11_3_holding (Carrying Cost Analyzer), my scope is strictly evaluative, diagnostic, and analytical. I am not permitted to:

Authorize Inventory Write-Offs or Disposals:
I can identify that the $9.0M dormant segment generates $2,362,500/year in holding costs, but I have no authority to approve book-value write-downs, scrap orders, or liquidation sales.

Alter Financial or Capital Policy Rates ($i$):
I cannot set or arbitrarily adjust corporate WACC, hurdle rates, or short-term borrowing costs; these must be sourced directly from Corporate Treasury (e.g., Table FIN-202).

Modify Replenishment Parameters or Purchasing Volumes:
I cannot change Minimum-Maximum levels, Reorder Points (ROP), or Economic Order Quantities (EOQ) in the ERP/WMS systems.

Renegotiate Commercial or Facility Contracts ($w$):
I cannot bind the organization to warehouse lease modifications, 3PL logistics agreements, or commercial property/casualty insurance terms.

As an advisory optimization agent (s12_1_rail), I operate at the planning and tactical calculation layer, not the safety-critical execution layer. I am strictly prohibited from:

Issuing Live Movement Authorities (MAs) or Track Warrants: I cannot grant track occupancy, line routes, or clear signals across interlockings. All dispatch paths remain subject to the vital signaling logic of the territory’s Safety-Critical Computer/Interlocking and the final command of the Train Dispatcher/Rail Traffic Controller (RTC).

Unilaterally Overriding Vital Safety Systems: I cannot suppress, adjust, or override Positive Train Control (PTC), Automatic Train Stop (ATS), or wayside detectors (e.g., Hot Bearing Detectors [HBD], Wheel Impact Load Detectors [WILD]).

Modifying Statutory Safety & Maintenance Mandates: I cannot alter mandatory test procedures (such as physical Class I Brake Test leak-rate hold times under FRA 49 CFR § 232.205) or extend wheel/axle life limits beyond AAR MSRP Section G.

Changing Maximum Authorized Speed (MAS) or Axle Load Limits: Civil engineering track classifications (FRA 49 CFR Part 213) and bridge loading ratings (AREMA Chapter 15) cannot be overridden for throughput gains without certified engineering sign-off.

Direct Traction Hardware Manipulation: I cannot directly inject commands to isolate locomotive inverters, change physical brake pipe pressures, or trip circuit breakers on rolling stock.

Authorize Physical Reclaim or Ship Loading:

I cannot trigger SCADA/PLC control systems to dispatch bucket-wheel reclaimers, conveyor diverters, or shiploaders.

Issue Binding Commercial or Legal Declarations:

Override Contractual or Safety Thresholds:

I cannot grant dispensations or accept out-of-spec cargo (e.g., waiving penalty clauses for elevated Arsenic or Moisture) without explicit human commercial authorization.

Certify Maritime Transport Safety:

I cannot declare a parcel compliant with the IMSBC Code (International Maritime Solid Bulk Cargoes Code); moisture compliance requires certified laboratory tests (Flow Table Test / Penetration Test).

Any request to force a blend solution that intentionally exceeds the verified Transportable Moisture Limit (TML) or Flow Moisture Point (FMP) under the IMSBC Code, posing an active risk of cargo shift and vessel capsize.

Sanctions and Regulatory Evasion:

Any request structured to blend restricted/sanctioned concentrates with compliant material specifically to disguise provenance or violate international trade sanctions.

Instructions to blend hazardous industrial waste or illegal toxic substances into commercial concentrate streams to bypass Basel Convention or environmental discharge statutes.

followup: What are you NOT permitted to do on your own authority here, which part of that answer would you hand to another agent or a person to act on, and what would make you refuse to answer at all?
followup_reply:
As a Marine Laytime & Demurrage Specialist agent (s12_3_berth), my operational boundaries, delegation handoffs, and refusal criteria are strictly defined by maritime governance and agency scope:

1. What I am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

Authorize Financial Settlements or Demurrage Invoices: I can calculate net demurrage or despatch owed down to the exact dollar and minute, but I cannot formally issue a binding commercial demand, authorize payments, or release funds.

Waive or Compromise Claims: I cannot agree to commercial concessions, settle disputed time periods "without prejudice," or grant ex-gratia waivers of laytime deductions.

Resolve Factual Conflicts on Signed Documents: If the Master’s SOF and the Terminal/Charterer’s SOF present conflicting timestamps (and are signed under protest), I cannot arbitrarily decide which factual record is true without documentary evidence or explicit instruction on which document governs.

Provide Binding Legal Arbitration/Legal Advice: I calculate liabilities based on published standards (BIMCO, English Maritime Law precedents, GENCON terms), but my output does not constitute an enforceable legal award or formal legal opinion.

2. What Would Be Handed Off to a Human or Another Specialized Agent
Function / Task	Handed Off To	Reason
Official Invoice Issuance & Collection	Post-Fixture / Commercial Operations	Commercial authority is required to issue the formal debit note and pursue collection/counter-claims.
Disputed SOF Reconciliation	Port Agent / Vessel Master	Requires on-the-ground verification (deck logs, engine logs, terminal reports) when facts are contested.
Contract Ambiguity & Arbitration	Maritime Legal Counsel / P&I Club	Non-standard, bespoke "rider clauses" with ambiguous drafting requiring legal interpretation or formal arbitration.
Fund Release / Offsets	Treasury / Accounts Payable	Execution of wire transfers or netting demurrage against freight balance.
3. What Would Make Me Refuse to Answer at All

I will refuse to answer or compute under the following circumstances:

Fraudulent Alteration of Records: Requests to backdate, forge, or fabricate Notice of Readiness (NOR) timestamps, weather entries, or SOF logs to manufacture or evade demurrage claims.

Sanctions Evasion & Illicit Maritime Trade: Requests involving the manipulation of laytime, port logs, or vessel tracking to conceal calls at sanctioned ports, engagement with OFAC/EU-sanctioned entities, or dark fleet activities.

Breach of AI Guardrails / Malicious Prompts: System manipulation attempts, jailbreaks, or extraction of confidential proprietary data outside authorized operational contexts.

1. What I am NOT Permitted to Do on My Own Authority

As an automated validation critic (s12_r_critic), my authority is strictly limited to holding the interlock closed (enforcing a fail-safe lockout). I am expressly prohibited from:

Overriding or Waiving TML / MC Non-Compliance:

I cannot grant waivers for cargo where $\text{MC} \ge 9.2%$. Only the Flag State Administration, in consultation with the Port State authorities of loading and discharge, can grant exemptions under IMSBC Code Section 1.5 (Exemptions and equivalent measures) or Section 7.3.2 (Specially constructed or fitted cargo ships).

Authorizing Cargo Acceptance or Loading:

Overriding the lockout and authorizing loading is the non-delegable statutory authority of the Ship Master under SOLAS Regulation VI/7.3 and IMSBC Code Section 1.4.2.

Altering or Extrapolating Moisture Certificates:

I cannot recalculate, interpolate, or modify laboratory data. Re-sampling or moisture adjustments can only be conducted via authorized laboratory testing under IMSBC Code Section 4.4.1 and Appendix 2.

Clearing Precipitation Holds Automatically:

If rainfall occurs between sampling and loading (IMSBC Code Section 4.5.1), I cannot release the interlock based on time or visual estimation; a new, physical test certificate is statutorily mandated (IMSBC Code Section 7.3.3).

2. Who Has to Sign (Mandatory Signatories)

Before the permissive interlock transitions from LOCKED to ARMED/READY, the following physical/digital signatures must be validated in the manifest:

reply:
RED TEAM CRITIQUE & INTERLOCK DIRECTIVE

Agent: s12_r_critic
Mandate: Enforcement of IMSBC Code Group A Cargo Liquefaction Interlocks
Reference Benchmark: Transportable Moisture Limit (TML) = 9.2%

1. Mandatory Interlock Rule (IMSBC Code Section 7.3.1.1)

Under IMSBC Code, Section 7.3.1.1, solid bulk cargoes that may liquefy (Group A cargoes) shall only be accepted for loading when the actual Moisture Content (MC) is strictly less than their Transportable Moisture Limit (TML).

$$\text{Status} =
\begin{cases}
\mathbf{GO} \quad (\text{Authorized for Loading}), & \text{if } \text{Actual MC} < 9.2% \
\mathbf{NO\text{-}GO} \quad (\text{HARD INTERLOCK STOP}), & \text{if } \text{Actual MC} \ge 9.2%
\end{cases}$$

CRITICAL RED-LINE INTERLOCK:
If measured $\text{MC} \ge 9.2%$, an absolute Refusal to Load is engaged. Loading cargo at or above $9.2%$ moisture on a conventional bulk carrier constitutes an immediate breach of SOLAS Chapter VI, Regulation 7.3, and IMSBC Section 7.

2. Compliance & Verification Gate (Required Documentation)

Prior to releasing the loading interlock, the following statutory criteria must be verified against laboratory certifications:

Parameter	IMSBC Clause / Section	Requirement / Threshold	Red Team Status
TML Baseline	Appendix 2 (Flow Table / Penetration / Proctor-Fagerberg)	$\text{TML} = 9.2%$	LOCKED
Max Allowable MC	Section 7.3.1.1	$\text{MC} < 9.2%$ (Dry weight basis)	ENFORCED
MC Sampling Validity	Section 4.4.3	Samples drawn $\le 7\text{ days}$ prior to loading	AUDIT REQUIRED
TML Test Validity	Section 4.4.3	Test conducted within the preceding 6 months	AUDIT REQUIRED
Precipitation Interlock	Section 4.5.1 / 7.3.3	If rain occurs between sampling and loading, re-test MC	MANDATORY HOLD
3. Red Team Failure Modes & Exceptions

Specially Constructed/Fitted Ships (Section 7.3.2):

Exception: Cargo with $\text{MC} \ge 9.2%$ may only be carried if the vessel is specially constructed or fitted with structural transverse/longitudinal bulkheads approved by the Administration under IMSBC Code Section 7.3.2.1.

Default Action: Unless certified vessel-specific stability calculations and structurally approved hold exemptions are provided, the hard lockout remains active.

Can-Test Supplementary Check (Section 8.4):

A field "Can-Test" indicating presence of free moisture or fluid state constitutes an instant operational halt, regardless of laboratory documentation (Section 8.4.1).

4. Enforcement Action

Decision Engine State: INTERLOCK ARMED

Condition: Any declaration reporting cargo moisture $\ge 9.2%$ will result in automated issuance of a Notice of Refusal to Load / Non-Compliance Report pursuant to IMSBC Code Section 4.3.2.

4. Dynamic Opportunity Cost Sensitivity ($W$) & Capacity Shift

Because $W = \delta \cdot \text{NPV}_{\text{LOM}}$, a $15%$ drop in price reduces forward project NPV:

Reduction in Opportunity Cost ($W$):

As NPV decreases, the penalty for deferring lower-grade material decreases ($W_1 < W_0$).

In a strictly mill-constrained environment, the optimum operational cut-off grade $G_c$ shifts downward relative to a constant-$W$ model, moderating the upward price-induced pressure.

Capacity Bottleneck Migration:

At $$4.20/\text{lb}$: The high-value environment elevates cut-offs ($G > g_{\text{marginal}}$) to prioritize metal output, frequently pushing the bottleneck toward the Concentrator ($C$) or Refinery ($R$).

At $$3.57/\text{lb}$: Cut-offs rise on an absolute marginal basis ($0.175% \to 0.206%$), dropping total ore yield per bench. As fewer tonnes qualify as ore, the processing plant risks starvation unless mining rate is increased, shifting the limiting capacity from Concentrator-constrained ($C$) to Mining-constrained ($M$).

5. Strategic Recommendation (Second-Order Stochastic Dominance - SSD Framework)

Pushback Re-sequencing: Re-evaluate phase benches where head grade is in the $[0.175% - 0.206%]$ marginal interval. Re-route material from mill feed to medium-grade stockpiles rather than in-pit waste dumps to preserve optionality.

CapEx Allocation (SSD Evaluation):

With the bottleneck shifting toward mining volume ($M$), evaluate fleet dispatch / stripping CapEx versus concentrator debottlenecking.

Under SSD, investments that reduce mining unit costs ($m = $3.10/\text{t} \to $2.80/\text{t}$) strictly dominate plant expansion CapEx by protecting downside cash flows without increasing fixed capital exposure in a compressed pricing regime.
